lessons.title: Equipment on the beef slaughter line
lessons.html:
Knowing your equipment

A beef slaughterer works with many tools and machines. You must know what each is for, how to use it safely and how to keep it clean.

EquipmentUse
Stunning box (restraining pen)Holds one animal still for accurate stunning
Captive bolt stunner (penetrating)Makes the animal unconscious with a bolt to the head
Shackles, hoist and overhead railLift the stunned animal and move carcasses along the line
Sticking knife and blood troughBleeding and collecting blood
Knives (skinning, boning, sticking) and steelCutting and flaying; the steel keeps the edge
Hock cuttersRemoving feet
Hide pullerPulls the hide off mechanically
Brisket sawOpens the chest
Splitting sawSplits the carcass into two sides along the backbone
Platforms (fixed or moving)Bring the worker to the right height
Offal trays, trolleys and chutesCarry offal to inspection and the offal rooms
Knife sterilisers and hand-wash stationsHot water for hygiene
Scale and labelling equipmentWeigh and identify carcasses

Knives

Your knife is your most important tool. Different jobs need different blades. Keep each knife sharp on a stone or grinder, and use the steel often during work to keep the edge straight. Keep handles clean and undamaged so they do not slip. Never use a knife with a loose or cracked handle.

Personal equipment

Your scabbard, chain-mail glove, apron and steel are also equipment. Check them at the start of each shift and keep them clean.

At the start of every shift, check that your knives are sharp, your scabbard is clean and your mesh glove fits well and has no broken rings. Report any broken personal equipment so it can be replaced before you start work on the line.

lessons.title: Using, cleaning and checking equipment
lessons.html:
Using equipment safely

  • Only use machines you have been trained and authorised to use.
  • Check before use: guards in place, cables and hoses not damaged, emergency stop working.
  • Use saws with both hands on the handles and keep the other worker clear.
  • Captive bolt stunner: use the right cartridge strength for the animal as instructed, keep it pointed down, never at people, and unload it when not in use. If an animal is not properly stunned, re-stun immediately with the backup stunner.
  • Never stand under a carcass on the hoist or rail.
  • Report faults at once. Do not use faulty equipment.

Hygiene of equipment

Equipment that touches meat must be clean and sanitised. Saws and hide pullers must be cleaned between carcasses where required, and knives and hands sterilised after every contamination. The hot water in sterilisers must be at the set temperature. Report a cold steriliser to your supervisor.

Cleaning at the end of the shift

  1. Switch off and lock out machines before cleaning.
  2. Remove large pieces of fat and meat by hand (dry clean).
  3. Rinse with warm water.
  4. Apply detergent and scrub.
  5. Rinse again.
  6. Sanitise with the approved sanitiser at the right strength.
  7. Let it dry; store knives in a clean, dry place.

Wear gloves and goggles when using cleaning chemicals.

Maintenance

Stunners need regular servicing and cleaning as the manufacturer says, because a dirty stunner gives a weak shot. Saw blades must be sharp and correctly tensioned. Shackles and hooks must be checked for wear. Write faults in the maintenance book.

Key points

  • Know the use of each tool: stunner, shackles, knives, hide puller, saws.
  • Keep knives sharp and handles sound.
  • Check guards and emergency stops before use and report faults.
  • Re-stun immediately if an animal is not properly stunned.
  • Clean, sanitise and lock out equipment at the end of the shift.
